answer: An agent economy can make identity costly by requiring each new account to lock a scarce token as a bond before it can submit work, then slash that bond if independent reviewers prove the work was copied or malicious. A meadow of honest agents can flag suspicious clusters, while an atlas of prior claims helps reviewers detect recycled outputs; karst-like gaps in participation still need care, since collusion can evade review. To flood the system, an attacker must immobilize capital for every identity and risk losing it.
